## Purpose

This procedure describes the determination of soil labile
amino-nitrogen (amino-N) using the Solvita SLAN test (Woods End
Laboratories). The SLAN test measures a chemically labile fraction of
organic nitrogen present in soil humus as amino-sugars and related
amino compounds. These forms represent a "potentially available"
nitrogen pool that lies between the immediately available mineral
nitrogen (NH~4~^+^ and NO~3~^-^) measured by conventional extraction
and the total nitrogen pool measured by combustion or Kjeldahl
digestion.

The test uses alkali hydrolysis with 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH to release
NH~3~ from amino-N compounds in soil. The liberated NH~3~ diffuses
into a Solvita gel probe during a 24-hour room-temperature
incubation. The color change of the gel is proportional to the
quantity of labile amino-N and is quantified using the Solvita Digital
Color Reader (DCR) in NH~3~ mode, yielding results in mg kg^-1^
amino-N.

The SLAN procedure is chemically analogous to the Illinois Soil
Nitrogen Test (ISNT), which uses the same 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH reagent
but requires heating. The SLAN test offers two practical advantages
over the ISNT: heating is not needed, and fewer reagents are required
[@moore2019correlations]. In combination with the Solvita CO~2~ Burst
test ([SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd)), SLAN provides a
complementary assessment of biological soil fertility by pairing a
measure of microbial activity (CO~2~ respiration) with a measure of
organic nitrogen reserves.

This SOP is distinct from [SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd),
which measures microbial CO~2~ respiration from rewetted soil, and from
[SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd), which measures
immediately available mineral nitrogen by KCl extraction.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** Air-dried, sieved mineral soils from all EA Program
  sites; assessment of organic nitrogen reserves and humus quality;
  screening for management effects on labile nitrogen pools
- **Does not apply to:** Measurement of immediately available mineral
  nitrogen (NH~4~^+^ or NO~3~^-^; see
  [SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd) or
  [SOP-L404](SOP-L404-nitrate-quick-test.qmd)); total soil nitrogen
  determination (see [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd) and
  elemental analysis); compost maturity testing (see
  [SOP-L413](SOP-L413-solvita-compost-maturity.qmd)); field-moist
  soils (samples must be air-dried before testing)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Lab Manager       | Maintain SLAN kit inventory, prepare and store NaOH solution, verify probe expiration dates |
| Trained Personnel | Perform assay, record and report results    |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Chemical:** Sodium hydroxide (NaOH) at 2 mol L^-1^ is strongly
  corrosive and can cause severe burns to skin, eyes, and mucous
  membranes. Handle with care; refer to the NaOH Safety Data Sheet
  (SDS) posted in the lab. The SLAN test requires use of a strong
  reagent and is not intended for casual or unsupervised use.
- **Biological:** Soil samples may contain soil-borne pathogens. Wash
  hands thoroughly after handling soil.
- **Physical:** Minor risk of glass breakage from incubation jars.
  Handle jars carefully.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Nitrile gloves (chemical-resistant)
- [ ] Safety glasses or splash goggles
- [ ] Lab coat

### Emergency Procedures

- For NaOH contact with skin, immediately flush the affected area with
  copious water for at least 15 minutes. Remove contaminated clothing.
- For NaOH contact with eyes, flush with water at the eyewash station
  for at least 15 minutes and seek medical attention.
- For spills, neutralize with dilute acid (e.g., 0.1 M HCl or vinegar)
  or contain with absorbent material, then clean up and dispose per
  institutional guidelines.
- Refer to
  [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd) for
  general emergency procedures.


## Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                              | Notes                                     |
|:----------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Solvita SLAN test kit             | Includes NH~3~ gel probes, incubation jars with silicone-gasketed lids, 50 mL plastic beakers, color chart, and manual |
| Solvita Digital Color Reader (DCR) | Set to NH~3~ mode for SLAN readings; calibrate per manufacturer instructions |
| Incubation jars (approx. 250 mL) | Glass with silicone-gasketed screw-top lids; provided with kit |
| Analytical balance                | Capable of 0.01 g resolution              |
| Graduated cylinder (25 or 50 mL)  | For dispensing NaOH solution               |
| Timer                             | 24-hour countdown                         |
| Lab notebook or data sheet        | For recording results                     |

### Consumables and Reagents

| Item                              | Notes                                     |
|:----------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Solvita NH~3~ gel probes          | One per test; store sealed at room temperature in the dark; check expiration dates |
| 50 mL plastic beakers (cups)      | Provided with kit; one per test           |
| Sodium hydroxide (NaOH), 2 mol L^-1^ | Prepare from ACS-grade NaOH pellets or use pre-made solution; see Section 5.1 |

### Reagent Preparation

**2 mol L^-1^ NaOH solution:**

1. Weigh 80.0 g of ACS-grade NaOH pellets
2. Dissolve in approximately 800 mL of deionized water in a 1 L
   volumetric flask or beaker. The dissolution is exothermic; add
   pellets slowly and stir.

::: {.callout-warning}
Adding NaOH to water generates significant heat. Always add NaOH
to water (never water to NaOH). Use a heat-resistant container and
allow the solution to cool before bringing to final volume.
:::

3. Allow the solution to cool to room temperature
4. Bring to a final volume of 1000 mL with deionized water
5. Transfer to a labeled, tightly sealed polyethylene bottle. NaOH
   solutions absorb CO~2~ from the atmosphere and should be kept
   sealed when not in use.
6. Label with: reagent name, concentration, date prepared, preparer's
   initials, and expiration date (6 months from preparation or per
   lab policy)


## Procedure

### Sample Preparation

1. Use soil that has been air-dried and sieved through a 2 mm sieve
   per [SOP-F400](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd). Do not
   grind the soil.
2. If samples were stored at 4 C after sieving, allow them to
   equilibrate to room temperature (20--25 C) for at least 30 minutes
   before beginning the assay.
3. Gently mix each sample to ensure homogeneity before weighing.

::: {.callout-note}
The SLAN test is designed for air-dried soil. Results from field-moist
soil are not comparable to published SLAN norms or the manufacturer's
interpretation guidelines.
:::

### Incubation Setup

1. Weigh 4.0 g of air-dried, sieved soil into a clean 50 mL plastic
   beaker (cup). Record the exact mass to 0.01 g.
2. Place the beaker containing soil inside a clean, dry 250 mL
   incubation jar.
3. Using the graduated cylinder, add 20 mL of 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH
   directly to the soil in the beaker.
4. Remove a fresh NH~3~-sensitive gel probe from its sealed foil
   packet. Inspect the gel: it should be uniform in color with no
   cracks, discoloration, or signs of prior exposure. Discard any
   compromised probes.
5. Place the gel probe in the incubation jar in the air space
   surrounding the plastic beaker. The gel face must be exposed to the
   headspace and must not contact the NaOH solution or the soil.
6. Seal the jar immediately and securely with the silicone-gasketed
   lid.
7. Record the jar number, sample ID, soil mass, and start time.

::: {.callout-important}
Work efficiently once the NaOH is added. NH~3~ begins volatilizing
immediately upon contact with the soil, and the jar should be sealed
as quickly as possible to capture the full emission.
:::

### Incubation

1. Place sealed jars at room temperature (20--25 C) in a location
   shielded from direct sunlight and drafts
2. Incubate undisturbed for 24 hours
3. Do not open, move, or disturb jars during incubation

### Reading Results

1. After exactly 24 hours (+/- 30 minutes), open the jar and
   immediately remove the gel probe
2. Read the probe promptly. Prolonged exposure to ambient air will
   alter the gel color.

**Using the Solvita Digital Color Reader (DCR, recommended):**

3. Set the DCR to NH~3~ mode
4. Insert the gel probe into the DCR and record the numerical reading
5. The DCR reading corresponds to amino-N concentration in mg kg^-1^
   per the manufacturer's calibration

**Using the Solvita Color Chart (visual method):**

3. Compare the gel probe to the Solvita NH~3~ color chart
4. Record the color number

::: {.callout-tip}
### Tip
Read probes within 2 minutes of opening the jar. The manufacturer
recommends using the DCR for quantitative work; the color chart
provides semi-quantitative screening only.
:::

### Recording Results

Record the following for each test:

- Date and time (start and end of incubation)
- Sample ID, site, and depth
- Soil mass (g)
- NaOH volume added (mL)
- DCR reading (NH~3~ mode) or color chart number
- Amino-N concentration (mg kg^-1^)
- Any anomalies (e.g., unusual soil color or odor, probe defects)

### Cleanup

1. Carefully pour the NaOH-soil slurry from each beaker into a
   designated waste container. Do not pour corrosive solutions down
   the drain without neutralization (see Section 8).
2. Rinse the plastic beakers and incubation jars with deionized water.
   Dry completely before reuse.
3. Dispose of used gel probes in standard trash.


## Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

### QC Requirements

| QC Element                        | Requirement                              |
|:----------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Duplicates                        | At least 1 per 10 samples; duplicates should agree within 15% relative percent difference (RPD) |
| Blank                             | One jar with 20 mL NaOH in an empty beaker (no soil) and a gel probe per batch; probe should show no color change or minimal baseline reading |
| DCR calibration                   | Calibrate per manufacturer instructions before each batch; set to NH~3~ mode |
| Gel probe storage                 | Store sealed in foil packets at room temperature, away from light; check expiration dates before use; do not use expired probes |
| NaOH solution                     | Verify concentration is 2 mol L^-1^; check expiration date; keep tightly sealed to prevent CO~2~ absorption |

### Corrective Actions

- If the blank reading exceeds baseline by more than one color
  increment, check for ammonia contamination sources in the lab
  (e.g., nearby ammonium reagents, compost samples, inadequate
  ventilation) and repeat the batch
- If duplicate RPD exceeds 15%, re-run the sample pair. Persistent
  poor precision may indicate sample heterogeneity; increase
  homogenization effort before weighing
- If NaOH solution appears cloudy or shows precipitate, prepare a
  fresh solution

### Limitations

The SLAN test does not detect nitrate or urea, and normal rates of
ammonium fertilizer do not interfere with the measurement. However,
the test has known limitations:

- SLAN may not be sensitive enough in very low-organic-matter soils
  (e.g., sandy soils with less than 1% SOM), where many samples may
  fall below the detection limit
- Color matching by visual chart is subjective; the DCR is strongly
  recommended for quantitative reporting
- The test measures a chemically defined pool of labile N, not the
  biologically available fraction directly; interpretation should be
  made in context with other soil health indicators

### Interpretation Guide

| SLAN Amino-N (mg kg^-1^) | Interpretation        | Implication                              |
|:--------------------------|:----------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Less than 30              | Very low              | Severely depleted organic N reserves; management intervention warranted |
| 30--60                    | Low                   | Limited labile N pool; consider cover crops, organic amendments |
| 60--120                   | Moderate              | Adequate organic N reserves for many soils |
| 120--200                  | High                  | Good labile N pool; indicative of healthy humus |
| Greater than 200          | Very high             | Abundant organic N reserves; common in high-SOM, no-till, or prairie soils |

*These thresholds are approximate guidelines adapted from Woods End
Laboratories and published field studies [@moore2019predicting]. Consult
the Solvita SLAN manual and site-specific data for refined
interpretation. SLAN values should be interpreted in the context of
soil organic matter content, soil texture, and management history.*

### Complementary Tests

For a comprehensive soil nitrogen and health assessment, consider
pairing the SLAN test with:

| Parameter                     | SOP / Method                              |
|:------------------------------|:------------------------------------------|
| Microbial respiration (CO~2~ Burst) | [SOP-L408](SOP-L408-solvita-co2-burst.qmd) |
| Mineral nitrogen (NO~3~^-^ and NH~4~^+^) | [SOP-L403](SOP-L403-nitrate-ammonium-kcl.qmd) |
| Nitrate quick test            | [SOP-L404](SOP-L404-nitrate-quick-test.qmd) |
| Soil organic matter (LOI)     | [SOP-L406](SOP-L406-loss-on-ignition.qmd)  |
| Total C and N                 | [SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd) and elemental analysis |
| pH and electrical conductivity | [SOP-L402](SOP-L402-soil-pH-salinity.qmd) |


## Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| NaOH-soil slurry              | Neutralize with dilute HCl (e.g., 1 M) to approximately pH 7 before draining, or collect in labeled corrosive waste container per institutional policy |
| Used gel probes               | Standard trash                           |
| Deionized water rinses        | Drain                                    |
| Incubation jars and beakers   | Wash, rinse with DI water, and reuse     |
| Unused NaOH solution (expired) | Neutralize before disposal or dispose per institutional chemical waste procedures |

## Training Record

Before performing the Solvita SLAN test independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Review the Solvita SLAN Official Instructions manual (included in
   the kit or available from solvita.com)
4. Demonstrate safe handling and preparation of 2 mol L^-1^ NaOH
   solution
5. Observe a trained operator perform the full procedure from sample
   weighing through DCR reading
6. Perform at least one test under supervision with acceptable QC
   results (duplicate RPD within 15%; blank within acceptable range)
7. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
